title: Potato Biological Lexicon — Canonical Literal Meanings
purpose: Prevent metaphor from flattening distinct botanical structures and mechanisms.

terms.definition: A swollen underground stem-derived storage and vegetative-propagation organ.
A lateral stem that grows underground; a stolon tip can transition into a tuber.
A node-associated bud complex on the tuber containing meristematic tissue.
A shoot growing from a tuber bud.
A true root arising from stem/shoot tissues after plant establishment.
Protective secondary dermal tissue comprising phellem, phellogen and phelloderm.
A multicellular opening/structure in periderm that facilitates gas exchange and can be a pathogen entry site.
terms.not: a stomatal pore with guard-cell control

terms.definition: Living ground tissue that makes up much of tuber flesh and contains abundant amyloplasts/starch.
A non-pigmented plastid specialized for starch synthesis and storage.
Vascular tissues arranged within the tuber that connect it to transport networks.
A tissue exporting assimilates/resources at a particular developmental stage.
A tissue importing and using/storing assimilates at a particular developmental stage.
A tuber or viable tuber piece planted for clonal propagation.
Botanical seed formed after sexual reproduction in potato berries.
Potato fruit containing true seeds; it is not the edible tuber.
Internally imposed inability of a bud/meristem to grow.
External environmental restraint of a growth-competent bud.
Suppression by another organ or signal within the organism.
Developmental readiness/history-dependent state of a tuber, not simply elapsed chronological time.
Four homologous chromosome sets derived within a species lineage; many cultivated potatoes are 2n=4x=48.
A linked chromosome sequence inherited as a unit; the four homologs of a tetraploid cultivar can have different haplotypes.
Number of copies of an allele among homologous chromosome copies.
Autopolyploid meiotic outcome in which related chromatid segments can enter the same gamete following multivalent recombination.
A representation of genomic diversity across multiple individuals/accessions rather than one linear reference genome.
Soil/microbial niche closely associated with underground stem/tuber surfaces.
Soil region influenced by roots and root exudates.
Microbial communities living within plant tissues.
Microbial habitat associated with above-ground plant surfaces.
A hydrophobic cell-wall-associated biopolymer central to periderm and wound barriers.
Developmental transition in which a stolon region changes growth program and becomes a tuber.
An FT-like mobile tuberigenic signal central to potato tuberization networks.
Accumulation of reducing sugars during cold storage through starch/sucrose remodeling, strongly involving vacuolar invertase.
Potato defense metabolites including alpha-solanine and alpha-chaconine; excessive levels are undesirable for food safety.

invariant_rules: Never call the edible tuber a root as literal botany.
Never use seed, seed tuber and true potato seed interchangeably.
Never treat 12×4 as four identical copies of each chromosome.
Never describe genotype as sufficient to determine phenotype without environment and developmental state.
Never infer project metaphysics from biological analogy.
